exposure: Timing of delivery (36, 37, or 38 weeks of gestation)
cohort: The study included 431 pregnant women with placenta previa who gave birth at 36, 37, or 38 weeks, with a median age of 36 years.
finding: Delivery can be safely delayed until the 38th week of pregnancy in placenta previa patients, except in cases of significant vaginal bleeding, as no significant differences in maternal outcomes were found between delivery timing groups, though birth weights and NICU admissions differed significantly.
birth_weight: Yes, birth weights differed significantly between groups (p<0.001).
gest_age: Yes, deliveries occurred at 36, 37, or 38 weeks of gestation.
